free_tier.stated: USD 90 Free Credits (Valid for 3 Months) for Elastic Compute Service, a one-time free tier per user
free_tier.notes: the ECS pricing page https://www.alibabacloud.com/en/product/ecs/pricing lists Reserved Instances, Pay-As-You-Go and Subscription and states no free allowance; its Free Trial link leads to https://www.alibabacloud.com/free; the pricing URL answers HTTP 200 on a direct request but ended at https://www.alibabacloud.com/en/notfound through one fetch egress, so the URL can answer differently by request origin; the Free Trial page https://www.alibabacloud.com/free was read through a browser-rendering provider (a plain read returned an empty shell)

limits.value: free trial is USD 90 of credit valid for 3 months, one-time for each user, open only to new users of ECS and Simple Application Server, with a credit or debit card required on the account; PayPal is not accepted

identity_cost.detail: a credit card or debit card must be added as a payment method during the free tier period; PayPal is not supported for the free tier, and only one account per user is eligible

confidence_note: the USD 90 ECS credit, its 3-month validity and the card requirement are stated on the Free Trial page https://www.alibabacloud.com/free; the ECS pricing page states no allowance of its own

extras.price_note: a VPS bills by the month with an hourly rate capped at the monthly figure, so the two columns answer two questions: destroying the box between runs versus keeping it up.
extras.price_basis: 10 h/day column = 300 h at the hourly rate, which is what a server destroyed between runs costs; 24/7 column = the monthly cap, because a VPS kept up all month stops at the cap.
